original_text: Seed Development Development: Programmed series of stages from a simple to a more complex form Development of a eudicot embryo nAfter double fertilization, the zygote divides repeatedly to form a proembryoand a suspensor
explanation: Development is a programmed series of structural and functional changes from simple to complex forms. In eudicot seeds, following double fertilization, the diploid zygote undergoes repeated cell division to form two structures: the proembryo (which will develop into the plant embryo) and the suspensor (which anchors the embryo and transfers nutrients to it).

questions.q: In eudicot seed development, what two structures are directly formed by the division of the zygote?
questions.exp: The zygote divides repeatedly to form a proembryo (the precursor to the embryo) and a suspensor.
